operations.details_summary: Callbacks can be asynchronous, reordered, or omitted by selected flags; callback presence alone is not complete request evidence.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WINHTTP_STATUS_CALLBACK primary official Microsoft source verified.
Defines callback parameters for WinHTTP handle, status, context, and status-specific information.
Callback data is transient and pointer lifetimes are status-specific; it must be copied safely and joined to the exact handle and request.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WINHTTP_ASYNC_RESULT primary official Microsoft source verified.
Carries asynchronous WinHTTP API and error information for request-error notifications.
An asynchronous error record identifies an API failure but does not by itself identify root cause, endpoint, process ownership, or recovery success.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WinHttpGetProxyForUrl primary official Microsoft source verified.
Resolves proxy information for a URL using explicit auto-proxy options and returns proxy and bypass data.
Proxy resolution may use cached PAC, WPAD, DNS, DHCP, or credentials and does not prove the proxy used by a later request.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WinHttpGetProxyForUrlEx primary official Microsoft source verified.
Starts asynchronous proxy resolution for a URL using a proxy-resolver handle created from an asynchronous WinHTTP session.
Starting proxy resolution only yields pending work; callback completion, result extraction, error status, and exact request application are required.

Evidence is accepted only with exact WinHTTP session/connection/request handle hierarchy, URL and proxy readback, TCP endpoint and owning process, TLS protocol and cipher, remote certificate digest and SSL chain policy, HTTP status/header/body byte count and digest, task, attempt, time window and four receipt correlation.
WinHttpGetIEProxyConfigForCurrentUser primary official Microsoft source verified.
Retrieves the current user's Internet Explorer or WinINet proxy and auto-configuration settings.
Current-user settings may not apply to service, scheduled-task, system, or explicitly configured WinHTTP contexts.

WinHttpGetDefaultProxyConfiguration primary official Microsoft source verified.
Retrieves the default WinHTTP proxy configuration.
Default proxy configuration is global configuration metadata and does not prove which proxy an individual request actually used.

WINHTTP_AUTOPROXY_OPTIONS primary official Microsoft source verified.
Defines PAC URL, auto-detection, and authentication behavior used by proxy resolution.
Auto-proxy options describe requested discovery behavior; they do not prove PAC integrity, discovery source, selected proxy, or request routing.

Proxy strings can contain multiple entries and bypass patterns; they require normalization and exact request-option readback.
